input.quote: Neither Party may assign, transfer or subcontract any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by the other Party. MSL may assign or subcontract all or any part of this Agreement to any MSL Related Company with IBM's prior written consent which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM.
input.rationale: Section 16.2 imposes a blanket prohibition on assignment by IBM without MSL's prior written approval, with no affiliate carve-out and no successor/M&A carve-out, and no reasonableness standard on MSL's approval of an IBM assignment. That is our walk-away position and fails the fallback as well (no successor assignment right on written notice for either party). The only reasonableness standard runs in MSL's favour, for assignments to an MSL Related Company. Section 16.5 (p0290) helpfully requires any acquirer of MSL to assume the Agreement, and the Loan Agreement general clause (p1578) restricts MSL only, so neither is flagged. There is no change-of-control termination right anywhere in the document, but nothing affirmatively confirms this, so we state it expressly. Our single inserted sentence pair cures the Customer-side carve-outs at the preferred level while leaving MSL's assignments subject to IBM's approval; MSL's existing prohibition already satisfies the Vendor-consent element.

proposal.summary: Add IBM affiliate/successor assignment carve-out, no MSL termination on IBM change of control, bar on MSL assigning to an IBM competitor, and a reasonableness standard on IBM's approval of other MSL assignments.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 16.2 bars assignment by IBM without MSL's approval with no affiliate or M&A carve-out, which is our walk-away position. We have added the customary IBM affiliate/successor rights, confirmed that an IBM change of control gives MSL no termination right, and kept MSL's assignments subject to IBM's approval (not unreasonably withheld) and off-limits to our competitors.

ops.text: IBM may assign this Agreement without MSL's approval to an affiliate of IBM or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all of its assets, and no change of control of IBM shall give MSL any right to terminate this Agreement. MSL may not assign this Agreement to any competitor of IBM, and IBM's approval of any other assignment by MSL shall not be unreasonably withheld.

mappings.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
mappings.quote: MSL may not assign or transfer any rights or duties under this Agreement without prior written approval by IBM.

mappings.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
